Vouch

VOWCH -- one syllable, rhymes with 'couch'. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To vouch to confirm that something is true, especially based on one's own experience.

My neighbor vouched for the contractor, having watched him rebuild her porch beam by beam.

Worked Example

When the new intern is stopped at the studio gate, the veteran producer walks over and tells the guard, 'I know this young man personally -- he is exactly who he says he is.'

Putting her own credibility on the line to confirm the intern's identity is what it means to vouch for someone. To vouch for a person or claim is to back it with your own firsthand experience and reputation.

How Vouch Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

confirm

confirm: to state or show that something is true

corroborate

corroborate: to support a claim with additional evidence

certify

certify: to declare something true officially

Antonyms

deny

deny: to declare that something is untrue

disavow

disavow: to refuse to accept responsibility for or support of something

How Strong Is It? — confirm → vouch → certify

confirm vs. vouch

confirm vs. vouch: Confirm is flatter and more impersonal than vouch -- a database can confirm a fact, but when you vouch for someone, you stake your own reputation on the truth of what you are saying.

certify vs. vouch

certify vs. vouch: Certify is more official than vouch: to vouch for something is a personal guarantee based on firsthand experience, while to certify is to declare it true formally, often with documents, seals, or legal weight.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — vouch-/voc-

root — vouch-/voc-: to call (Latin vocare, via Old French voucher 'to summon')

Put it together

Put it together: Vouch traces through Old French voucher, 'to summon,' back to Latin vocare, 'to call.' In medieval courts, to vouch was to call a person in to stand behind a claim -- and over time, to vouch for something came to mean calling yourself as its witness.

Use the root in a new word: vocation

Use the root in a new word: vocation: Teaching turned out to be her true vocation, the work she felt called to do.

Root Check

Word Choice

Vouch is nearly always followed by 'for': you vouch for a friend, vouch for a product, vouch for the truth of a story. What makes vouching different from simply agreeing is the personal stake -- you are offering your own experience and reputation as the guarantee.
